reasoning_traces.think:
The four-factor model originates from Dean Oliver’s foundational work, where eFG%, TOV%, TRB%, and FTr are treated as statistically independent variables that jointly predict team success. The SUR approach allows for simultaneous regression of these factors, capturing their interdependencies without assuming independence. Each factor is modeled as a linear function of player actions, with coefficients derived from historical data. The unit-improvement equivalence implies that a one-unit increase in offensive efficiency (e.g., eFG%) has the same marginal impact on win probability as a one-unit decrease in defensive inefficiency (e.g., TOV%). This duality enables a unified metric space for evaluating both offensive and defensive contributions. Failure modes include omitted variable bias due to non-linear interactions, and overfitting from small sample sizes. The model assumes normality of residuals and homoscedasticity, which may not hold under extreme performance variations.
